speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The classic presentation of brief, spontaneous episodes of vertigo lasting less than a minute (though your patient reported 3 minutes, which is slightly atypical but consistent with a severe episode or a vestibular paroxysm), absence of auditory symptoms, and lack of central neurological deficits (normal speech, no weakness, no facial droop) strongly points to a peripheral etiology. Given the high probability of BPPV or a vestibular migraine, I will not order further imaging as the MRI is expected to be negative; instead, I recommend performing the Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis and identify the specific canal involved.
